title: Factorization through Lorentz cones
summary: A pair of proper cones $(\mathsf{C}_1,\mathsf{C}_2)$ is said to have the Lorentz factorization property (LFP) if every $(\mathsf{C}_1,\mathsf{C}_2)$-positive map factors through a direct sum of Lorentzian cones, i.e., cones over Euclidean balls. Clearly, $(\mathsf{C}_1,\mathsf{C}_2)$ has the LFP if either $\mathsf{C}_1$ or $\mathsf{C}_2$ is a direct sum of Lorentzian cones, and our main goal is to find other examples.
